description: Read about inquiry drafts, browser storage and product information on the LZZ website. The form creates an email draft without sending or uploading files.
mainText: Privacy & site informationInformation about inquiry drafts, browser storage and the product details on this site.Your inquiryThe form creates an email draft in your browser. It does not send your information to LZZ or upload drawings. To contact us, open the draft in your email app, add your attachments and send it yourself.Saved draftsThe form saves your input and draft status in the current tab using sessionStorage, with a separate entry for each selected part. Your details stay available after a refresh but are not saved to an account or sent to LZZ. Select "Clear saved input" to remove the entry for the current part.Your browser may restore this data when it restores a previous session. Clear your input before leaving a shared device. If browser storage is blocked or full, you can still use the form while the page is open. Select "Save draft" to download a text copy.Cookies and external servicesThis site does not use analytics or advertising cookies. Your email provider, WhatsApp and other linked websites have their own privacy policies.Product and company informationProduct pages use catalog photographs and clearly labeled illustrative visuals. Neither is an inspection record or a specification document. Original workshop photographs and company documents are identified separately from product examples.Product pages use shorter titles and summaries of the catalog entries. Original catalog names and source material are retained in our archive; they are not displayed on every product page. The summaries are not independently verified specifications for the photographed parts. Confirm material grades and tolerances with the team, along with the inspection and commercial terms for your order.The engineering guides help you prepare an inquiry; they are not inspection records or customer case studies. They do not establish suitability for a particular application. Material filters help you find existing parts without creating duplicate product pages. English descriptions of company documents explain their contents but do not verify current validity.ContactFor questions, contact roger@lzz-cnc.com.

When does a part need more than one process?A shaft with cross-holes, a turned fitting with milled flats or a housing with angled faces may need more than one operation or setup. The route should preserve the relationships between critical features. Send a 3D model and controlled 2D drawing so the team can review datums, access and inspection together. Is 5-axis machining always more accurate?No single process label guarantees accuracy. Acceptance depends on the part geometry, machine and setup, datum strategy, material, finishing and measurement method. If an interface matters, state its tolerance and datum on the drawing and ask how it will be produced and checked. Any tolerance target needs feature-specific review. Mark the surfaces that locate, seal, slide or carry load on the drawing so you can discuss tolerances in relation to their function.Compare milled pockets and housings with turned shafts and fittings. Include a controlled 2D drawing when these requirements apply.Tolerances need review against the specific drawing. The material and feature geometry affect the assessment, as do the setup and measurement method; a single tolerance cannot apply to every catalog part. Agree on inspection requirements and supporting records for your design. Specify material and finishState the exact alloy or plastic grade and any material-certificate requirement. For coated parts, specify the finish and whether critical dimensions apply before or after treatment. Mark areas that need masking, cosmetic faces and burr-sensitive edges.The material and finish checklist covers these details. Catalog photographs show shapes and surfaces; they cannot establish a coating specification or provide material certification. Agree on prototype checksExplain the purpose of the prototype.
